title: Singapore Manufacturing Port Operations Control Tower
thesis: Snowflake turns daily berth data from Meranti Quay Terminals, a fictional Singapore container terminal operator serving the export network of the fictional manufacturer Halcyon Components (mainline, feeder, transshipment, barge and reefer berths across six Singapore port districts), into on-time box-move KPIs, 7-day berth disruption-risk scores, vessel waiting-time anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables.

talking_points: On-time box moves, berth disruptions, rehandle moves and box moves handled for 30 berths across Tuas, Pasir Panjang, Tanjong Pagar, Pioneer, Sembawang and Changi.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it can be traced back to berth-day rows and the vessel calls behind them.
The late-box-moves chart shows which disruption causes push the most moves outside the agreed berth window.
show: Late box moves by disruption cause
tabs.call_out: One governed set of berth KPIs, traceable to source rows

transition.line: Which berths are likely to cause the next disruption?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification scores each berth's probability of a disruption in the next 7 days.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent labelled days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags vessel waiting-time outliers per berth, and the forecast projects port-network box moves for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

transition.line: How healthy are the cranes behind those risks?

talking_points: Crane uptime and crane readiness (ship-to-shore, tandem-lift, mobile harbour and barge cranes, and reefer monitoring racks) frame the response capacity.
Crane PM compliance against on-time box moves by berth shows where maintenance discipline and berth-window performance move together; it is an association, not proof of cause.
The action memo drafts three prioritised actions from the KPI, disruption, cause and risk tables only.
show: PM compliance vs on-time box moves
tabs.call_out: Grounded draft actions, with a human in the loop

transition.line: What happens when a berth raises a vessel-waiting alarm right now?

talking_points: Live quay sensor readings (vessel waiting hours, berth occupancy) land in RAW.LIVE_TELEMETRY, from the simulator or from AWS IoT Core through Snowpipe.
The Snowflake alert logs ALARM readings with an SOP hint and the berth's current risk band, then emails the Meranti Quay berth duty manager.
tabs.call_out: From alarm to action in one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent uses Cortex Analyst over the semantic view for metrics, and Cortex Search over synthetic berth SOPs.
Each answer shows the generated SQL and the SOPs it cited.

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: Two builds share one core: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake (IoT Core, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q).
Everything shown is synthetic demo data, rebuilt reproducibly from the repo.
tabs.call_out: One governed core, with an optional AWS edge
